reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only addresses computational modeling of HEA structural properties and nanoindentation hardness of bulk as-cast HEAs; it provides no support for the key premises about laser cladding process characteristics, HAZ reduction, hot-cracking mitigation, or the feasibility of depositing a crack-free HEA overlay.
premises: Laser cladding with rapid solidification can produce a fine microstructure and minimal HAZ in the deposited material.
A fine microstructure and minimal HAZ reduce the formation of brittle interdendritic phases that cause hot cracking.
HEA formulations (e.g., CoCrFeNiAl) can be deposited as an overlay via laser cladding.
The resulting HEA overlay will be metallurgically bonded and crack-resistant.
